Chapter 2: Rewriting the Money Mindset
Now that you’ve spotted the barriers standing in your way, let’s talk about how you can actually change the way you think—and feel—about money.
The stories we tell ourselves about money? They shape everything. These stories usually come from our upbringing, our culture, and all those past experiences we carry with us.
Sometimes, those old beliefs end up holding us back—without us even noticing. For example, you might have heard that money is always scarce, or that wanting more somehow makes you selfish. Maybe it feels like real financial success is only for other people.
Here’s the thing: these ideas can sneak into your decisions every day. You might hold back from asking for a raise because you’re worried you’ll come across as ungrateful. Or maybe you avoid investing because it just seems too risky, or maybe even too complicated.
The first step to changing all of this? Awareness. Start paying attention to those automatic thoughts that pop up whenever you think about money. Where do they come from? Are they really true, or just old habits? And most importantly—are they helping you grow, or keeping you stuck?
Imagine your mind as a garden. Those old, limiting beliefs? They’re like weeds. Once you spot them, you can start to pull them out. And in their place, you plant seeds of new beliefs—ones that encourage abundance, confidence, and self-worth.
Of course, this isn’t an overnight transformation. It’s a practice, and it takes patience and kindness with yourself along the way.
So, how do you actually nurture a healthier money mindset? Start by reflecting on your financial goals and dreams—not just the bills in front of you. Give yourself permission to think bigger.
Then, try surrounding yourself with stories of women who’ve already achieved financial success. It really does help expand your sense of what’s possible.
Practice gratitude for what you have, while also making space to want more. There’s nothing wrong with ambition and desire.
And when you hit a setback, reframe it. Instead of seeing it as proof you’ve failed, treat it as a chance to learn and grow.
Of course, money isn’t just about numbers—it’s deeply emotional. Feelings like guilt, shame, or fear might pop up when you start going after more. That’s totally normal. But those emotions don’t have to run the show. When you acknowledge them and move forward anyway, you’re building real resilience and confidence.
Here’s another important point: your self-worth and your net worth? They’re not the same thing. Money is just a tool—it doesn’t define your value as a person. When you can separate who you are from how much you have, you’ll find it’s easier to make bold moves and worry less about making mistakes.
As you shift your mindset, your actions start to change too. Suddenly, you’ll spot opportunities where you only saw obstacles before. You’ll feel more ready to invest in yourself, ask for what you deserve, and take smart risks. And honestly, this new perspective? It’s the real foundation for building lasting wealth.
